| [CLAIM-830](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-830.md) v2 | The mean-field derivation of the Barabási–Albert power law is the age mechanism in logarithmic time, so what separates linear preferential attachment from Gibrat's lognormal growth is the continual entry of new units and not the proportionality of growth | Fills a gap in the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws". A says that linear preferential attachment "involves proportional expected growth" (A3 §4), contrasts it with Gibrat growth, which gives a lognormal, and separately gives the age mechanism (A5 §6), but never connects the two. In logarithmic time a Barabási–Albert node grows as e^(a/2), where a = ln(t/t_i) is its log-age. Uniform births make a exponential with rate 1, so P(K ≥ k) = k^(−1/(1/2)) = k^(−2), which is Reed's s^(−λ/g). Proportional growth is common to both. Entry is what makes the Pareto: without it, linear attachment among fixed nodes is a Pólya urn with a near-exponential spread in the long run (Barabási and Albert's Model B shows a power law only transiently; see the revision of 2026-11-22). Checked by simulation with python3 -I: log-ages have mean 1.000, the CCDF slope is −1.98, and the 100 largest hubs were all born in the first 1% of the growth. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
